# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** 30 to 35 years old  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario (by family heritage) / Vancouver  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and writer  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## Appearance

He is tall and broad-shouldered, with thick brown hair, a finely-cut nose and chin, and large, brilliant dark-gray eyes. He knows how to dress well, though he looks as though life has not been entirely easy for him.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)_

## Personality

He possesses a pleasant voice and a delightful smile. He inspires trust and confidence easily in others, naturally inspiring people to confide in him. Passionate and emotionally expressive, he deeply appreciates scenery, art, and natural beauty.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018)_

- Pleasant voice and delightful smile  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>

- To write a great Canadian novel  <sub>[v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>
- To court and marry Leslie Moore  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001)</sub>

## History

Following a severe bout of typhoid fever in the spring, Owen Ford was advised by his doctor to recuperate by the sea. He traveled to Four Winds to visit the original home of his maternal grandparents. While there, he befriended Anne Blythe, Gilbert Blythe, and Captain Jim Boyd. After hearing Captain Jim's life experiences, Owen agreed to collaborate with him on writing a biographical book. During his stay, he fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore. Recognizing her difficult marriage, he initially confessed his feelings to Anne and left Four Winds to avoid causing trouble. He completed the life-book, titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim', which was accepted for publication. He later returned from Vancouver to Four Winds to court Leslie after her circumstances changed.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018), [v4 c28 P35](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0035), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Selwyn, the schoolmaster who built the house Anne and Gilbert lived in  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Suffered a severe case of typhoid fever in the spring  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Worked as a journalist and magazine short story writer  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## Quotes

> And so this is Four Winds. I wasn’t prepared to find it quite so beautiful, in spite of all mother’s praises. What colors—what scenery—what charm! I shall get as strong as a horse in no time. And if inspiration comes from beauty, I should certainly be able to begin my great Canadian novel here.  <sub>[v4 c23 P18](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0018)</sub>

> We’ll collaborate. You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>
